pp:me:2016:q4-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 4
pp:me:2016:q4-s2.question: A function  of the Complex Variables z=x+iy, is given as f(x,y)=u(x,y)+i v(x,y) , where u(x,y)=2kxy and v(x,y)=$x^{2}-y^{2}$.  The value of k, for which the function is analytic, is _____

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given that $( f(z)=u+i v)$ is analytic

$$\begin{aligned} u(x, y) &=2 k x y & & v=x^{2}-y^{2} \\ u_{x} &=2 k y & & v_{y}=-2 y \\ u_{x} &=v_{y} & & \\ k &=-1 & & v_{x}=2 x \\ u_{y} &=2 k x & & & \\ u_{y} &=-v_{x} & & & \\ 2 k x &=-2 x & & & \\ k &=-1 & & \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q6-s2.question: A point mass having mass M is moving with a velocity V at an angle $\theta$ to the wall as shown in the figure. The mass undergoes a perfectly elastic collision with the smooth wall and rebounds. The total change (final minus initial) in the momentum of the mass is

pp:me:2016:q9-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 9
pp:me:2016:q9-s2.question: The forces F1 and F2 in a brake band and the direction of rotation of the drum are as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction is 0.25. The angle of wrap is $3\pi /2$ radians. It is given that R = 1 m and F2 = 1 N. The torque (in N-m) exerted on the drum is _________

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} F_{1} &>F_{2} \\ \frac{F_{1}}{F_{2}} &=e^{\mu \theta} \\ \frac{F_{1}}{F_{2}} &=e^{0.25 \times \frac{3 \pi}{2}} \\ F_{1} &=F_{2} \cdot e^{0.25 \times \frac{3 \pi}{2}} \\ &=1 \times e^{0.25 \times \frac{3 \times \pi}{2}} \\ &=3.2482 \mathrm{N} \\ \text { Torque } &=\left(F_{1}-F_{2}\right) \times r \\ &=(3.2482-1) \times 11 \\ &=2.2482 \mathrm{Nm} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q10-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 10
pp:me:2016:q10-s2.question:
A single degree of freedom mass-spring-viscous damper system with mass m, spring constant k and
viscous damping coefficient q is critically damped. The correct relation among m, k, and q is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given : 1. single degree of freedom 2. Mass =m 3. Spring constant =k 4. Damping coefficient =q 5. Critically damped Damping factor =1 Correct relation: Damping factor = $$\begin{array}{c}\ \frac{\text { Damping coefficient }}{2 \times \text { mass } \times \text { Natural frequency of vibration }} \\ 1=\frac{q}{2 \times m \times \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}} \\ q=2 \sqrt{km} \end{array}$$

a point at the center at location Y
a point on the circumference at location X
a point at the center at location X

pp:me:2016:q15-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 15
pp:me:2016:q15-s2.question: A hollow cylinder has length L, inner radius $r_{1}$, outer radius $r_{2}$, and thermal conductivity k. The thermal resistance of the cylinder for radial conduction is

detailed_solution.markdown: $Q=\frac{\Delta T}{\text { Thermal resistance }}$ Thermal resistance $=\int_{t_{1}}^{t_{2}} \frac{L}{k A}$ $$\begin{aligned} \quad&=\int_{t_{1}}^{r_{2}} \frac{d r}{k \times 2 \pi r l} \\ \quad&=\frac{1}{2 \pi / k} \int_{r_{1}}^{r_{2}} \frac{d r}{r} \\ \quad&=\frac{1}{2 \pi l k}[\ln r]_{r_{1}}^{r_{2}} \\ \quad&=\frac{1}{2 \pi l k} \ln \frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}} \\ \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q16-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 16
pp:me:2016:q16-s2.question: Consider the radiation heat exchange inside an annulus between two very long concentric cylinders. The radius of the outer cylinder is $R_{0}$  and that of the inner cylinder is $R_{i}$ . The radiation view factor of the outer cylinder onto itself is

detailed_solution.markdown: To find: Radiation view factor of the outer cylinder onto itself. Hence $F_{11}$ is required. $$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow A_{1} F_{12}&=A_{2} F_{21} \qquad[\text { Reciprosity }]\\ F_{11}+F_{12}&=1 \qquad \text { [Summation] }\\ F_{21}+F_{22}&=1\\ \therefore \quad F_{11}&=1-F_{12} \\ F_{22}&=0 \text { [No radiation leaving }\\ &\text{surface 2 reaches back to 2]}\\ \therefore \quad F_{21} &=1 \\ F_{12} &=\frac{A_{2}}{A_{1}} \times F_{21}=\frac{A_{2}}{A_{1}} \times 1 \\ &=\frac{2 \pi R_{i} L}{2 \pi R_{0} L} \times 1=\frac{R_{i}}{R_{0}} \\ F_{11} &=1-F_{12}=1-\frac{R_{i}}{R_{0}} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q19-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 19
pp:me:2016:q19-s2.question: Consider a simple gas turbine (Brayton) cycle and a gas turbine cycle with perfect regeneration. In both the cycles, the pressure ratio is 6 and the ratio of the specific heats of the working medium is 1.4. The ratio of minimum to maximum temperatures is 0.3 (with temperatures expressed in K) in the regenerative cycle. The ratio of the thermal efficiency of the simple cycle to that of the regenerative cycle is _________

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Given: }r_{p}&=6\\ y&=1.4 \end{aligned}$$

$\frac{T_{\max }}{T_{\min }}=0.3 \quad$ [for regenerative cycle ]

$$\begin{aligned} \eta_\text { Tregenerative cycle } &=1-\frac{T_{\max }}{T_{\min }} \times\left(r_{p}\right)^{(\gamma-1) / \gamma} \\ &=1-0.3\times(6)^{\frac{0.4}{1.4}}\\ &=0.49945 \times(6)^{\frac{0.4}{1.4}} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \eta_{\text {simplecycle }} &=1-\frac{1}{\left(r_{p}\right)^{(\gamma-1) / \gamma}} \\ &=1-\left(r_{p}\right)^{(1-\gamma) / \gamma} \\ &=1-(6)^{-\frac{0.4}{1.4}}=0.4066 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text { Required ratio } &=\frac{\eta_{\text {simple cycle }}}{\eta_{\text {regenerative cycle }}} \\ &=\frac{0.40666}{0.49945}=0.8141 \end{aligned}$$

By Trapezoidal

$\int_{0}^{\pi}(\sin x+\cos x) d x=\frac{\pi / 3}{2}(1+(-1)+$

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mechanics - Impulse and Momentum, Energy Formulations
detailed_solution.markdown: $E_{\text {intial }}-E_{\text {brake }}=E_{\text {final }}$ $\frac{1}{2}l\omega_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} m v_{1}^{2}+m g H_{1}-E_{\mathrm{brake}}$ $=\frac{1}{2} I \omega_{2}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} m v_{2}^{2}+m g H_{2}$ $E_{\mathrm{brake}}=\frac{1}{2} I \omega_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} m v_{1}^{2}+m g\left(H_{1}-H_{2}\right)$ $H_{1}-H_{2}=0.5 \mathrm{m}$ $E_{\mathrm{brake}}=\frac{1}{2} I \omega_{1}^{2}+m g h+\frac{1}{2} m v_{1}^{2}$ $=\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times 150 \times 2^{2}+2000 \times 9.81 \times 0.5+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2000 \times 2^{2}}{1000}}{1000}$ $=14.11 \mathrm{kJ}$

The position of the particle with respect to G is given by the vector $\rho _{i}$ . The time rate of change of the angular momentum of the system of particles about G is

pp:me:2016:q33-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 33
pp:me:2016:q33-s2.question:
A simply supported beam of length 2L is subjected to a moment M at the mid-point x = 0 as shown in the figure. The deflection in the domain $o\leq x\leq L$ is given by
$w=\frac{-Mx}{12EIL}(L-x)(x+c)$
where E is the Young's modulus, I is the area moment of inertia and c is a constant (to be determined)

The slope at the center x = 0 is

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Torsion of Shafts
detailed_solution.markdown: Equation of deflection $$\begin{aligned} W &=\frac{-M}{12 E I L}\left[L x^{2}-x^{3}+L c x-C x^{2}\right] \\ \frac{d W}{d x} &=\frac{-M}{12 E I L}\left[2 L x-3 x^{2}+L C-2 C x\right] \\ \frac{d^{2} W}{d x^{2}} &=\frac{-M}{12 E I L}[2 L-6 x-2 C] \\ \therefore \quad E I \frac{d^{2} W}{d x^{2}} &=\frac{-M}{12 L}[2 L-6 x-2 C] \\ \text { now } \quad E I \frac{d^{2} W}{d x^{2}} &=\frac{-M}{12 L}[2 L-6 x-2 C]\\ \text{at }\quad x&=L, M_{x}=0 \\ \therefore \quad C&=2 L\\ Slope\\ \frac{d W}{d x} &=\frac{-M}{12 E I L}\left[2 L x-3 x^{2}+2 L^{2}-4 L x\right] \\ \therefore \quad \left|\frac{d W}{d x}\right|_{x=0} &=\frac{-M L}{6 E I} \end{aligned}$$

The stress (in Pa) in the link AB is ___________

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mechanics - FBD, Equilirbium, Plane Trusses and Virtual work
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \Sigma F_{v}&=0 \\ and \quad \Sigma F_{x}&=0[\text { At equilibrium }]\\ F_{B C} \sin 45^{\circ}&=F_{A B}+P \sin 45^{\circ} \\ \text { for } \Sigma F_{v}&=0 \\ F_{B C} \cos 45^{\circ} &=P \cos 45^{\circ} \text { for } \Sigma F_{x}=0 \\ \therefore \quad F_{B C}&=P \\ P \sin 45^{\circ}&=F_{A B}+P \sin 45^{\circ} \\ \therefore F_{A B} &=0 \\ \sigma_{A B} &=0 \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q35-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 35
pp:me:2016:q35-s2.question:
A circular metallic rod of length 250 mm is placed between two rigid immovable walls as shown in the figure. The rod is in perfect contact with the wall on the left side and there is a gap of 0.2 mm between the rod and the wall on the right side. If the temperature of the rod is increased by $200^{\circ}C$ , the axial stress developed in the rod is __________ MPa
Young's modulus of the material of the rod is 200 GPa and the coefficient of thermal expansion is $10^{-5}per^{\circ}C$

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Stress and Strain
detailed_solution.markdown:
Free expansion of rod$=L \alpha \Delta T$

$$\begin{aligned} &=250 \times 10^{-5} \times 200\\&=0.5 \mathrm{mm} \\ \text { Actual expansion } &=0.2 \mathrm{mm}\\ \therefore \quad \text{Expansion resisted} &=0.3 \mathrm{mm} \\ \therefore \quad \text{Strain resisted } &=\frac{0.3}{250} \\ \text { Stress developed } &=\frac{0.3}{250} \times 200 \times 10^{3} \\ &=0.24 \times 10^{3}=240 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q36-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 36
pp:me:2016:q36-s2.question: The rod AB, of length 1 m, shown in the figure is connected to two sliders at each end through pins. The sliders can slide along QP and QR. If the velocity VA of the slider at A is 2 m/s, the velocity of the midpoint of the rod at this instant is ___________ m/s.

detailed_solution.markdown: $\omega _3=\omega _{AB}=\frac{V_A}{I_{13A}}=\frac{V_B}{I_{13B}}=\frac{V_C}{I_{13C}}$ $I_{13A}=$ Distance between $I_{13}$ and point A $I_{13B}=$ Distance between $I_{13}$ and point B $I_{13C}=$ Distance between $I_{13}$ and point C $\frac{V_A}{I_{13A}}=\frac{V_C}{I_{13C}}$ $\frac{2}{I_{13A}}=\frac{V_C}{I_{13C}}$ Applying sine law in triangle $ABI_{13}$ $$\frac{1}{\sin 120^{\circ}}=\frac{I_{13A}}{\sin 30^{\circ}} I_{13A}=\frac{\sin 30^{\circ}}{\sin 120^{\circ}} Applying sine law in ACI_{13}=0.5774 \begin{aligned} \frac{I_{13C}}{\sin 30^{\circ}} &= \frac{I_{13A}}{\sin 90^{\circ}}\\ I_{13C}&= \frac{I_{13A}\sin 30^{\circ}}{\sin 90^{\circ}}\\ &=0.5774 \times 0.5=0.2887m \\ V_C&=\frac{V_A I_{13C}}{I_{13a}} \\ &=\frac{2 \times 0.2887}{0.5774}=1 m/s \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q37-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 37
pp:me:2016:q37-s2.question: The system shown in the figure consists of block A of mass 5 kg connected to a spring through a massless rope passing over pulley B of radius r and mass 20 kg. The spring constant k is 1500 N/m. If there is no slipping of the rope over the pulley, the natural frequency of the system is_____________ rad/s.

detailed_solution.markdown: Total energy of system $$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}+\frac{1}{2} k x^{2}+\frac{1}{2} I \omega^{2} \\ &=\frac{1}{2} m\left(r \times \frac{d \theta}{d t}\right)^{2}+\frac{1}{2} K \times(r \theta)^{2} \\&+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{M r^{2}}{2} \times\left[\frac{d \theta}{d T}\right]^{2} \\ &=\frac{1}{2} M r^{2} \cdot(\dot{\theta})^{2}+\frac{1}{2} K \times r^{2} \theta^{2}+\frac{M r^{2}}{4}(\dot{\theta})^{2} \end{aligned}$$ since total energy remains constant with respect to time. $$\begin{aligned} \frac{d E}{d t} &=0 \\ \frac{d E}{d t} &=\frac{1}{2} m r^{2} 2 \cdot \dot{\theta} \ddot{\theta}+\frac{K r^{2}}{2} \cdot 2 \theta \cdot \dot{\theta}+\frac{M r^{2}}{4} 2 \dot{\theta} \dot{\theta} \\ 0 &=m r^{2} \dot{\theta} \ddot{\theta}+K r^{2} \theta \cdot \dot{\theta}+\frac{M r^{2}}{2} \dot{\theta} \ddot{\theta} \end{aligned}$$ Divide both sides by $\dot{\theta}$ $0=m r^{2} \ddot{\theta}+K r^{2} \theta+\frac{M r^{2}}{2}$ Divide both sides by $r^{2}$ $$\begin{aligned} 0 &=m \ddot{\theta}+K \theta+\frac{M \ddot{\theta}}{2} \\ 0 &=\left(m+\frac{M}{2}\right) \ddot{\theta}+K \theta \\ 0 &=\ddot{\theta}+\left[\frac{K}{m+\frac{M}{2}}\right] \theta \\ \omega_{n}^{2} &=\frac{K}{m+\frac{M}{2}} \\ \omega_{n} &=\sqrt{\frac{2 k}{M+2 m}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \times 1500}{20+(2 \times 5)}} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{3000}{20+10}}=\sqrt{100} \\ &=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q38-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 38
pp:me:2016:q38-s2.question: In a structural member under fatigue loading, the minimum and maximum stresses developed at the critical point are 50 MPaand 150 MParespectively. The endurance, yield, and the ultimate strengths of the material are 200 MPa,300 MPa and 400 MPa, respectively. The factor of safety using modified Goodman criterion is

detailed_solution.concept: Machine Design - Fatigue Strength and S-N Diagram
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned}  \sigma _{max}&=150MPa\\ \sigma _{min}&=50MPa\\ S_e&=200MPa\\ S_{yt}&=300MPa\\ S_{ut}&=400MPa\\ \sigma _a&=\frac{\sigma _{max}-\sigma _{min}}{2}\\ &=\frac{150-50}{2}\\ &=50 MPa\\ \sigma _m&=\frac{\sigma _{max}+\sigma _{min}}{2}\\ &=\frac{150+50}{2}\\ &=100 MPa\\ &\text{Goodman sequation}\\ \frac{\sigma _a}{S_e}+\frac{\sigma _m}{S_{ut}}&=\frac{1}{FS}\\ \frac{50}{200}+\frac{100}{400}&=\frac{1}{FS}\\ FS&=2 \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q42-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 42
pp:me:2016:q42-s2.question:
Consider a parallel-flow heat exchanger with area $A_{p}$  and a counter-flow heat exchanger with area $A_{c}$. In both the heat exchangers, the hot stream flowing at 1 kg/s cools from $80^{\circ}$C to $50^{\circ}$C .  For the
cold stream in both the heat exchangers, the flow rate and the inlet temperature are 2 kg/s and $10^{\circ}$C , respectively. The hot and cold streams in both the heat exchangers are of the same fluid.
Also, both the heat exchangers have the same overall heat transfer coefficient. The ratio  $A_{c}$/ $A_{p}$ is _________

detailed_solution.markdown: Parallel flow $A_{p} =$ Area of parallel flow heat exchanger Counter flow $A_{c}=$ Area of counter flow heat exchanger Heat lost by hot stream in both heat exchanger $$\begin{aligned} &=m c\left[T_{h i}-T_{h o}\right] \\ &=1 \times c \times\left[T_{h i}-T_{h o}\right] \\ &=1 \times c \times[80-50]=30 \mathrm{ckW} \end{aligned}$$ Heat gained by cold stream in both exchange $$\begin{aligned} &=m c\left[T_{co}-T_{c i}\right] \\ &=2 \times c\left[T_{c o}-10\right] \end{aligned}$$ Heat lost by hot stream = Heat gain by cool stream $$\begin{aligned} 30c &=2c(T_\infty -10) \\ T_\infty &= \frac{30}{2}+10\\ &=15+10=25^{\circ} C\\ A_P, LMTD&= \frac{\Delta T_i-\Delta T_e}{ln(\Delta T_i/\Delta T_e)}\\ &= \frac{70-25}{ln(70/25)}=43.705^{\circ} C\\ Q_H&=UA_P 43.705 \\ A_C, LMTD&= \frac{\Delta T_i-\Delta T_e}{ln(\Delta T_i/\Delta T_e)}\\ &= \frac{55-40}{ln(55/40)}=47.103^{\circ} C\\ Q_H&=UA_C 47.103 \\ \therefore \; UA_P 43.705 &=UA_C 47.103\\ \frac{43.705}{47.103}&=\frac{A_C}{A_P}=0.927 \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q43-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 43
pp:me:2016:q43-s2.question:
Two cylindrical shafts A and B at the same initial temperature are simultaneously placed in a furnace. The surfaces of the shafts remain at the furnace gas temperature at all times after they are introduced into the furnace. The temperature variation in the axial direction of the shafts can be assumed to be negligible. The data related to shafts A and B is given in the following Table.

The temperature at the centerline of the shaft A reaches $400^{\circ}$ C after two hours. The time required (in hours) for the centerline of the shaft B to attain the temperature of $400^{\circ}$ C is _______

detailed_solution.concept: Heat Transfer - Fins and Unsteady Heat Transfer
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} T_{(r, t)} &=T_{0}+\left(T_{\infty}-T_{0}\right) \operatorname{erf}(z) \\ \frac{T_{(r, t)}-T_{0}}{T_{\infty}-T_{0}} &=\operatorname{erf}(z) \\ \frac{T_{(r, t)}-T_{0}}{T_{\infty}-T_{0}} &=\operatorname{erf}(z) \end{aligned}$$

For shaft A $\quad \frac{T_{0.2, t}-T_{i}}{400-T_{i}}$

For shaft B $\quad \frac{T_{0.05, t}-T_{i}}{400-T_{i}}$

Hence error function of both shafts will be same.

$\therefore \qquad z_{A}=z_{B}$$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\Gamma_{A}}{2 \sqrt{\alpha_{A} t_{A}}} &=\frac{T_{B}}{2 \sqrt{\alpha_{B} t_{B}}} \\ \frac{\Gamma_{A}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{A} t_{A}}} &=\frac{\Gamma_{B}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{B} t_{B}}} \\ \frac{\Gamma_{A}^{2}}{\alpha_{A} t_{A}} &=\frac{r_{B}^{2}}{\alpha_{B} t_{B}} \\ t_{B} &=\left(\frac{r_{B}}{r_{A}}\right)^{2} \times \frac{\alpha_{A}}{\alpha_{B}} \times t_{A} \\ \alpha_{A} &=\frac{k}{\rho c_{p}}=\frac{40}{2 \times 10^{6}}=\frac{20}{10^{6}} \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{s} \\ \alpha_{B} &=\frac{k}{\rho c_{p}}=\frac{20}{2 \times 10^{7}}=\frac{1}{10^{6}} \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{s} \\ t_{B} &=\left(\frac{r_{B}}{r_{A}}\right)^{2} \times \frac{\alpha_{A}}{\alpha_{B}} \times t_{A} \\ &=\left(\frac{0.1}{0.4}\right)^{2} \times \frac{20}{10^{6} \times \frac{1}{10^{6}}} \times 2 \\ &=\frac{1}{16} \times 20 \times 2=2.5 \mathrm{hrs} \end{aligned}$$

pp:me:2016:q45-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 45
pp:me:2016:q45-s2.question: A reversible cycle receives 40 kJ of heat from one heat source at a temperature of $127^{\circ}$C and 37 kJ from another heat source at $97^{\circ}$C. The heat rejected (in kJ) to the heat sink at  $47^{\circ}$C is __________

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy
detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: $$\begin{aligned} T_{1} &=127^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=(127+273) \mathrm{K} \\ &=400 \mathrm{K}\\ T_{2} &=97^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=(97+273) \mathrm{K} \\ &=370 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{3} &=47^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=(47+273) \mathrm{K} \\ &=320 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ For reversible cycle Clausius inequality, $\oint \frac{S Q}{T}=0$ $$\begin{aligned} \therefore \qquad \frac{40}{400}+\frac{37}{370}-\frac{Q_{3}}{320}&=0 \\ 0.1+0.1&=\frac{Q_{3}}{320}\\ \text{or}\qquad Q_{3}&=64 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}$$

The partial pressure of water vapour in a moist air sample of relative humidity 70% is 1.6 kPa, the
total pressure being 101.325 kPa. Moist air may be treated as an ideal gas mixture of water vapour
and dry air. The relation between saturation temperature ($T_{s}$  in K) and saturation pressure ($p_{s}$  in KPa) for water is given by $ln(p_{s}/p_{o})$=14.317-5304/$T_{s}$ , where $p_{o}$ = 101.325 kPa. The dry

Relative humidity,

$\phi=70 \%=0.70$

Partial pressure,

Total pressure,

pp:me:2016:q49-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 49
pp:me:2016:q49-s2.question: Gray cast iron blocks of size 100 mm x 50 mm x 10 mm with a central spherical cavity of diameter 4 mm are sand cast. The shrinkage allowance for the pattern is 3%. The ratio of the volume of the pattern to volume of the casting is _________

detailed_solution.markdown:
Ratio of volume of pattern to volume of casting is given by

$=\frac{(1.03\times100)\times(1.03\times50)\times(1.03\times10)}{100\times50\times10}=1.093$

Volume of cavity is assumed to be small and negligible as it will complicate the question to a higher level.

If your answer was less than 1, read below.

There are three things to be understood here :-

1. Liquid Shrinkage

It refers to the reduction in volume when the metal changes from liquid state to solid state at the solidus temperature. The liquid shrinkage is rarely a problem, because the molten metal is continuously flowing in mold cavity and also riser to compensate the shrinkage of liquid in the cavity.

2. Solidification i.e Liquid to solid phase transformation (GCI expands in this process unlike other metals)

So now during phase transformation gray cast iron expands (unlike other metals which contract) and there is no need of riser (used to take care of phase transformation shrinkage + liquid shrinkage).

3. Solid state Cooling (GCI contracts in this process just like other metals)

It refers to the reduction in volume caused when metal loses temperature in solid state. To account for this, shrinkage allowance is provided on the patterns. The Shrinkage allowance depends primarily upon Coefficient of thermal expansion. For Grey CI in particular it is positive, it means solid grey cast iron expands on increasing temp and contracts on decreasing temperature just like any other metal.

Adding all above factors

Neglecting the Liquid shrinkage we see that GCI expands in during solidification and contracts when cooled in solid form. So the net result would be sum of them. According to NPTL in the table for GCI they have given the net value of shrinkage’s which is positive and hence the pattern size would be more than the casting.

Note: The expansion of GCI during phase change (solidification) is a fact but at the same time we need to consider the contraction of GCI when cooling in solid state. So net result according to IISC and NPTEL is contraction so the size of pattern will be more than that of casting.

pp:me:2016:q61-s2.title: GATE ME 2016 | Set 2 | Question: 61
pp:me:2016:q61-s2.question: Students taking an exam are divided into two groups, P and Q such that each group has the same number of students. The performance of each of the students in a test was evaluated out of 200 marks. It was observed that the mean of group P was 105, while that of group Q was 85. The standard deviation of group P was 25, while that of group Q was 5. Assuming that the marks were distributed on a normal distribution, which of the following statements will have the highest probability of being TRUE?
options: No student in group Q scored less marks than any student in group P.
No student in group P scored less marks than any student in group Q.
Most students of group Q scored marks in a narrower range than students in group P.
The median of the marks of group P is 100100.
